overview: White grabs space with 3.d5 before Black has committed to ...d5 or ...Bg7. Black normally plays 3...Bg7 4.Nc3 d6 5.e4 O-O and reaches a King's Indian Orthodox/Normal structure, or builds a Benoni-style game with ...c6 or ...c5; the ...b5 Adorjan Gambit is a rare try. White keeps a space edge and aims for e4, Nf3 and Be2, with a locked centre and queenside play; Black prepares ...e5 or ...c6 breaks. Most games transpose into familiar KID structures. The subtree also holds other anti-Grünfeld branches (3.f3, 3.h4) that are different systems.

white_ideas.idea: Take space with d5, e4 and a quick Nf3 and Be2, transposing to a favourable King's Indian
Keep the centre closed and play on the queenside with b4/c5 ideas
Meet the Adorjan ...b5 gambit by taking or ignoring it and keeping extra pawns

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto ...Bg7, ...d6, ...O-O and hit the centre with ...e5 or ...c6
Break with ...c6 or ...c5 to attack the d5 pawn and gain counterplay
Use the half-open e-file and later ...b5 to undermine the pawn chain

typical_structures.structure: White c4/d5/e4 chain against Black d6/e5 (King's Indian locked centre) or c5/d6 (Benoni-like)

character.notes: Black usually reaches a King's Indian or Benoni structure, which is double-edged, but 3.d5 itself is less forcing. I read it as Balanced with low confidence; Sharp is plausible.

gambit.notes: No material is given in the main continuation; ...b5 gambits are sublines.

soundness.notes: Sound for both; White gets a space edge, Black gets counterplay.

structure.notes: The pawn chain c4-d5 with a locked centre after ...e5 resembles the King's Indian, so Closed, though ...c6 or ...c5 setups would be Semi-open.

approach.notes: 3.d5 is a rare anti-KID/Grünfeld choice for strong players, who prefer 3.Nc3. Offbeat.

level.notes: Black needs KID-style judgement; there is little forced theory. Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Adorjan Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: Black sacrifices a pawn at once, a Benko-style gambit.

sublines_that_differ.name: Alekhine Variation (3.f3)
sublines_that_differ.how: A different White system, not an advance, shown here because the data groups it with this root.

sublines_that_differ.name: Basman-Williams Attack (3.h4)
sublines_that_differ.how: An unusual attacking try, far from the 3.d5 main line.

character.reason: Mostly King's Indian or Benoni-type positions after a quiet start, with no forced play early.

gambit.reason: No material is given in the main continuation.

soundness.reason: A reasonable space-gaining move that Black can meet in standard ways.

structure.reason: After ...d6 and ...e5 the centre locks as in the KID; ...c5 or ...c6 lines are Semi-open.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose 3.d5 over 3.Nc3 against the KID/Grünfeld.

level.reason: KID-like structures need judgement but there is little forced theory.

plans.reason: White grabs space and Black fianchettoes the g7 bishop.
